scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-03.statement: Field route completion for Aug-Sep is 0.88 (target 0.95)

interpretation_history.interpretation: Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 in June/July to ~1180 in August and 1260 in September, confirming a roughly two‑fold increase since August.
The observation shows disputed bills split by read type: 1,240 estimated and 1,785 actual. This indicates that disputes occur for both estimated and actual reads, with actual reads slightly higher.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating field manual read performance is insufficient and may be contributing to higher estimated reads and dispute tickets.

Route completion for August‑September remains 0.88, below the 0.95 target, showing that manual read performance is insufficient; however, the low completion is not linked to the surge in disputed estimated bills, which are primarily due to AMI reads rejected for high consumption.
Dispute response times are well within the SLA (median 1.6 days < 3 days), indicating that ticket handling speed is not a bottleneck despite the surge in volume.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating no tariff changes were logged during the observed period.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder SH-BILL states there has been no tariff change this year, indicating that tariff modifications are not a recent source of billing disputes.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field team is short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers. This staffing shortage can contribute to the increase in disputed bills and dispute tickets.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract clause indicates that the utility can request route priority changes, but such changes only take effect after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, showing that route adjustments are possible but require human approval.

interpretation_history.interpretation: MDMS export access being provisioned enables retrieval of AMI read events, which can improve billing accuracy and reduce reliance on manual reads, addressing part of the estimated bill driver.

The observation shows that the vast majority of disputed estimated bills stem from AMI reads taken before cutoff but rejected for high consumption, indicating a data‑validation issue rather than missing reads from field staffing shortage.
